newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hoechst has financing for Roussel offer.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst has financing for Roussel offer.

text.p: German chemicals conglomerate Hoechst has bank financing in place to pay for its offer to buy out minority shareholders in Roussel-Uclaf, Hoechst's finance director said on Wednesday.
"We have certainly made arrangements with a number of banks in order to be able to close the deal by the time we get there," Klaus Schmieder told a news conference here.

He gave no details on the financing terms, which were "certainly in place," but said they were at "attractive conditions." He added, "If you just look at interest rates these day, you'll get an idea."
Hoechst does not need to list HMR to reduce debt, he said.
The terms of the Clariant deal, announced on Tuesday, would result in a "de-leveraging of approximately 3.5-4 billion deustchemarks," he said.
"Take that amount and add what we will repay in '97; we will end up looking at a balance sheet at the end of 1997 which will show, by and large, the same type of leverage as at the end of 96."

"We will look at a 34 percent equity of total balance sheet, something we feel very comfortable with and will enable us to make a major move should the opportunity arise...The HMR IPO is not needed to put us back into a position of comfort," he said.
